date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                09 OCT 2026 5:59PM by PIB Delhi
content:
Union Minister for Food Processing Industries, Shri Chirag Paswan, today said that India’s food processing sector offers immense opportunities and has the potential to play a major role in generating employment, promoting entrepreneurship, strengthening farmers’ incomes and enhancing India’s global presence. Shri Paswan is the Union Minister for Food Processing Industries, while Shri Avinash Joshi is the Secretary of the Ministry.
Addressing the 7th Convocation of the National Institute of Food Technology Entrepreneurship and Management, Kundli (NIFTEM-K), Shri Paswan urged graduating students not to restrict themselves to becoming job seekers, but to emerge as job creators, innovators and solution providers. NIFTEM-K’s official portal also identifies the 2026 event as its 7th Convocation.
He said that despite the progress made in recent years, the food processing sector continues to offer enormous untapped potential. The sector can contribute simultaneously to better food quality, value addition, stronger economic opportunities for farmers, employment generation and reduction of food wastage.
Shri Paswan said India’s vast agricultural base, diversity of produce and large consumer market give the country the strength to emerge as a “Global Food Basket”. He underlined the need to take food value chains, processing facilities and technology closer to farms and rural areas so that the benefits of food processing reach producers at the grassroots.
Calling upon students to think beyond conventional pathways, he urged them to use technology, innovation and entrepreneurship to find solutions to emerging challenges. He assured young innovators that the Government would support new ideas and initiatives aimed at strengthening the sector.
The Minister also made a strong appeal for maintaining quality, stressing that there should be no compromise on quality in the food sector. He said that the quality of an Indian product affects not merely the reputation of an individual company, but also the standing of “Brand India” in global markets.
Secretary, Ministry of Food Processing Industries, Shri Avinash Joshi, highlighted the wider role of food processing in reducing food wastage, enhancing nutrition and value addition, creating livelihood opportunities and encouraging entrepreneurship. He emphasised the importance of developing skilled human resources and encouraging students and researchers to pursue ideas and innovations that can create value on a larger scale.
Dr. Trilochan Mohapatra, Chairman, Board of Governors, NIFTEM-K, emphasised that the knowledge and skills acquired by students should contribute not only to their individual careers but also to the progress of the country and society. NIFTEM-K officially lists Dr. Mohapatra as Chairperson of its Board of Governors.
He stressed the need to strengthen NIFTEM-K’s research, skilled human resource and innovation ecosystem, and called for disruptive innovations that could help India achieve global leadership in food technology, safe and nutritious food, sustainable processing and value addition. Joshi Sir Sec
NIFTEM-K Director Dr. Harinder Singh Oberoi said that the Institute has made significant progress in academics, research, infrastructure and industry partnerships.
A total of 260 students received degrees at the Convocation, comprising 140 B.Tech., 78 M.Tech., 18 MBA and 24 Ph.D. students. Eight meritorious students were awarded Gold Medals in recognition of their academic excellence and dedication.
Dr. Oberoi said that NIFTEM-K’s endeavour is to equip students not only with academic qualifications but also with capabilities in research, innovation, entrepreneurship and industry-oriented learning, enabling them to respond effectively to the evolving needs of the food sector.
Dr. R. S. Sodhi, President (Food and Agriculture), Reliance Retail Ltd., said that this was one of the most opportune times for professionals to enter India’s food sector. His current industry designation is President (Food and Agriculture), Reliance Retail Ltd.
Dr. Sodhi described food as a relatively recession-resilient sector, noting that while consumers may postpone several discretionary purchases, food remains an essential everyday requirement. He said that with a population of more than 1.4 billion and changing consumption patterns, India offers substantial opportunities across the food value-addition ecosystem.
Shri Deepak Agarwal, Chairman and Managing Director, Bikaji Foods International Limited, encouraged graduating students to make full use of emerging opportunities in the food industry and described them as the future of the sector. Bikaji’s official corporate information confirms Shri Agarwal as Chairman and Managing Director.
The speakers collectively underlined that NIFTEM-K’s role extends beyond academic education. As an institution connecting research, industry, entrepreneurship and Government, it has the potential to play an increasingly important role in strengthening India’s food processing ecosystem and nurturing the next generation of innovators, professionals and entrepreneurs.

title: Union Health Ministry to Observe World Mental Health Day 2026, Reaffirming Commitment to Accessible, Inclusive and People-Centred Mental Healthcare
subtitle:
​​​​​​​Tele-MANAS renders yeoman service in bringing free, confidential and round-the-clock mental health support within easy reach of people across India through toll-free helpline 14416

Over 47.75 lakh calls received since launch on 10 October 2022; 53 Tele-MANAS Cells operational across all 36 States and Union Territories

Women account for nearly 44% of recorded caller profiles, reflecting growing access to mental health support through telephone-based counselling

MANN Jaagriti initiative to strengthen community awareness, encourage early help-seeking and address mental health stigma

Mental health services integrated into over 1.83 lakh Ayushman Arogya Mandirs; District Mental Health Programme sanctioned for 767 districts
ministry: Ministry of Health and Family Welfare
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                09 OCT 2026 7:22PM by PIB Delhi
content:
The Ministry of Health and Family Welfare will observe
World Mental Health Day on 10 October 2026
, reaffirming the Government of India's commitment to making mental healthcare accessible, affordable, inclusive and people-centred. This year's global theme,
“Lived experiences heard: real voices, real change,”
underscores the importance of listening to individuals with lived experiences of mental health conditions and ensuring their voices contribute to shaping responsive mental health policies and services.
At the heart of India's efforts to improve access to mental healthcare is
Tele MANAS (Tele Mental Health Assistance and Networking Across States)
, which has emerged as an important pillar of the country's mental healthcare delivery system. Through its
national toll-free helpline 14416
, Tele-MANAS is providing free, confidential and round-the-clock mental health counselling and support, enabling people to seek professional assistance easily, irrespective of their geographical location or socioeconomic background.
Tele-MANAS: Making Mental Health Support Just a Phone Call Away
Launched on 10 October 2022, Tele-MANAS has rendered yeoman service in bridging gaps in access to mental healthcare by bringing timely counselling, emotional support and professional guidance directly to people through a simple telephone call.
Since its launch,
Tele MANAS has received 47,75,644 calls, with 53 operational cells across all 36 States and Union Territories
, as of October 2026. This extensive reach reflects the growing importance of accessible, technology-enabled mental health services in addressing diverse mental health needs across the country.
Through
14416
, individuals experiencing emotional distress, anxiety, stress, sleep-related concerns or other mental health challenges can connect with trained counsellors without having to travel to a healthcare facility for initial support. Available 24 hours a day, seven days a week, and supported by multilingual services, the helpline makes it easier for people to seek help at a time and place convenient to them.
The service is particularly significant for people residing in rural, remote and underserved areas, where access to specialised mental healthcare facilities may be limited. By offering a confidential and supportive platform, Tele-MANAS is also helping address hesitation associated with seeking mental health assistance and encouraging individuals to reach out early.
Beyond initial counselling, the programme facilitates access to specialised mental health professionals and appropriate referral services wherever required, helping ensure continuity of care through linkages with the wider public healthcare system.
Growing Public Engagement Reflects the Importance of Accessible Mental Healthcare
The increasing utilisation of Tele-MANAS highlights the importance of having a readily accessible platform where individuals can seek support without fear of stigma or discrimination.
An analysis of 13,35,275 recorded caller profiles indicates that
women account for 43.78% (5,84,587) of callers
, while men constitute 54.18% (7,23,427). The substantial participation of women highlights the role of telephone-based counselling in providing a convenient and supportive avenue for seeking mental healthcare.
The service has also witnessed significant engagement among young and working-age populations, with individuals aged
18–45 years accounting for 73.2% of recorded caller profiles
.
The range of concerns reported by callers, including emotional distress, stress related to examinations, workplaces and relationships, anxiety and sleep disturbances, demonstrates the importance of accessible mental health support in everyday life.
By providing a platform where individuals can speak openly, receive guidance and be connected to appropriate services, Tele-MANAS is contributing to a broader shift towards recognising mental health as an integral part of overall health and well-being.
MANN Jaagriti: Taking Mental Health Awareness to Communities
As part of World Mental Health Day 2026, the Ministry is also taking forward
MANN Jaagriti
, a structured community awareness and engagement initiative aimed at strengthening mental health literacy, reducing stigma and encouraging timely help-seeking.
The initiative seeks to move beyond one-time awareness activities by promoting sustained community engagement through schools, colleges, workplaces, health facilities and other community platforms.
Through locally relevant activities, States and Union Territories will encourage open conversations around mental health, promote early identification of mental health concerns and create greater awareness about available services, including Tele-MANAS.
The initiative will also encourage the involvement of healthcare professionals, educators, community workers, youth, families, caregivers, civil society organisations and persons with lived experience of mental health conditions.
By bringing mental health conversations into everyday community settings, MANN Jaagriti aims to foster supportive environments where seeking mental health assistance is recognised as a positive and important step towards well-being.
Strengthening Mental Healthcare from the Community to the District Level
Complementing the reach of Tele-MANAS, the Government of India continues to strengthen mental healthcare services through the
National Mental Health Programme (NMHP)
and the
District Mental Health Programme (DMHP)
.
The DMHP has been sanctioned for implementation in
767 districts
, with support extended to States and Union Territories under the National Health Mission. The programme facilitates outpatient care, counselling, psychosocial interventions, medicines, follow-up care, outreach activities and referral services, alongside provisions for inpatient mental healthcare at the district level.
Mental health services have also been integrated into the Comprehensive Primary Health Care package offered through
over 1.83 lakh Ayushman Arogya Mandirs
across the country.
Through these facilities, primary healthcare teams undertake screening and early identification of mental health concerns, provide psychosocial support and follow-up care, and facilitate referrals to higher healthcare facilities wherever necessary.
Together, these initiatives are strengthening a continuum of mental healthcare that connects community awareness, primary healthcare, district-level services and digital counselling platforms.
Towards a More Inclusive and Supportive Mental Healthcare Ecosystem
On World Mental Health Day 2026, the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare reiterates that
mental healthcare should be within everyone's reach and seeking help should never be a source of hesitation or stigma
.
The growing reach of Tele-MANAS, alongside the expansion of community-based and primary mental healthcare services, reflects the Government's continued efforts to build a responsive healthcare system that places the needs, dignity and well-being of individuals at its centre.
Through Tele-MANAS, the Ministry is reinforcing a simple but important message: mental health support need not be distant, difficult or inaccessible.
Help is available, and reaching out can begin with a phone call.
The Ministry encourages individuals experiencing mental health concerns, as well as families and caregivers seeking guidance, to make use of the free and confidential services offered through
Tele MANAS at 14416
, available 24×7 across the country.
Every conversation matters. Every voice deserves to be heard. And mental health support must be accessible to all.

title: National Medical Library Organises 5th ERMED Consortium National Training-cum-Conference on “Digital Health Resources: Redefining Access Through Libraries
subtitle:
Digital Health Resources Crucial to Building India’s Research Mindset: Smt. Punya Salila Srivastava, Secretary, Health

Union Health Secretary Calls for Expanding Digital Medical Resources to All Medical Colleges, Particularly in Underserved Areas

Digital Health Resources Must Translate Information into Evidence and Evidence into Better Healthcare: Dr. Lovneesh G. Krishna, DGHS

ERMED Conference Features Hands-on Training on Four Digital Platforms to Enhance Access to Medical Knowledge
ministry: Ministry of Health and Family Welfare
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                09 OCT 2026 12:15PM by PIB Delhi
content:
The National Medical Library (NML), Directorate General of Health Services (DGHS), Ministry of Health and Family Welfare, Government of India, organised the 5th One-Day National Training-cum-Conference on the ERMED Consortium today at the National Medical Library, New Delhi. The conference was held on the theme “Digital Health Resources: Redefining Access Through Libraries”, highlighting the growing importance of digital knowledge resources in strengthening healthcare delivery, medical education and evidence-based clinical practice.
The inaugural session was attended by Smt. Punya Salila Srivastava, Secretary, Ministry of Health and Family Welfare; Dr. (Ms.) Vinod Kotwal, Additional Secretary, Ministry of Health and Family Welfare, and Dr. Lovneesh G. Krishna, Director General of Health Services.
Addressing the gathering, Smt. Punya Salila Srivastava, Secretary, Ministry of Health and Family Welfare, underscored the pivotal role of the National Medical Library (NML) in facilitating access to knowledge and information and strengthening the foundations of medical education, research and healthcare delivery. She highlighted the expansion of the NML network to 93 medical colleges and emphasised the need to extend its reach to all medical colleges across the country, particularly those in underserved areas, to ensure equitable access to quality medical literature and digital learning resources.
Emphasising that continuous learning and professional development are indispensable in the medical field, she observed that healthcare is evolving rapidly, with new diseases being identified, innovative therapies emerging and clinical practices continually advancing. She noted that well-equipped libraries and accessible digital resources are essential to strengthening professional competence and enabling healthcare practitioners to provide the best possible care to patients.
She further emphasised that digital health resources are not merely tools for accessing information but also vital enablers of a strong research culture in the country. Referring to the vision of the Hon’ble Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi, she stressed the importance of developing India’s indigenous research capabilities and cultivating a scientific temper that encourages innovation and original inquiry.
She also observed that while India may draw upon research conducted elsewhere, its larger aspirations cannot be realised without developing its own research capabilities and mindset. As she emphasised, “We may be able to manage with research conducted elsewhere, but that alone cannot fulfil our resolve to build a strong research ecosystem of our own. For this, we must develop a research mindset, and access to digital health resources is crucial to nurturing that mindset.” In this context, she highlighted the complementary role of the
One Nation One Subscription
initiative and the ERMED Consortium in broadening access to scholarly publications, facilitating evidence-based learning and creating an enabling environment for research and innovation. She described the National Medical Library as a legacy institution with the responsibility of serving as a gateway to knowledge and contributing meaningfully to the vision of Viksit Bharat.
Looking ahead, Smt. Srivastava called upon the National Medical Library to develop a comprehensive roadmap for strengthening access to digital health resources, including exploring the role of artificial intelligence in healthcare education, research and professional development. She emphasised the importance of extending guidance and support to States and Union Territories by facilitating the exchange of knowledge and the adoption of good medical library practices across institutions. She encouraged the organisation of focused seminars and professional engagements to identify effective models, share best practices and improve the accessibility and utilisation of digital educational resources nationwide.
Expressing confidence in the deliberations of the conference, she urged librarians, healthcare professionals and other participants to contribute their experiences, insights and actionable recommendations towards building a more accessible, inclusive and research-oriented medical knowledge ecosystem. She emphasised that empowering medical institutions with reliable knowledge resources and fostering a culture of lifelong learning would be instrumental in advancing medical education, strengthening research and improving patient care across the country.
Speaking at the Occasion, Dr. (Ms.) Vinod Kotwal, Additional Secretary, Ministry of Health and Family Welfare, highlighted the unique nature of knowledge, noting that while material wealth diminishes when spent, knowledge grows when shared. She observed that libraries are rooted in this very ethos of knowledge-sharing and emphasised the importance of leveraging digital resources to make quality medical and educational content more accessible to all. She noted that the three essential pillars of a medical college are its faculty, infrastructure and knowledge resources, including books, journals and other scholarly materials, all of which play a vital role in strengthening medical education and research.
Dr. Kotwal underscored the importance of ensuring that digital educational resources are not merely available but are also accessible and useful to medical practitioners, researchers and students. She exhorted librarians and participants attending the conference to actively engage in the deliberations, share their experiences and provide constructive feedback and practical insights to help improve the quality, relevance and accessibility of digital knowledge resources. She emphasised that such collective efforts would help medical libraries respond more effectively to the evolving learning and research needs of the healthcare community.
Dr. Lovneesh G. Krishna, Director General of Health Services (DGHS), highlighted the changing role of libraries in the digital era, noting that they are evolving from physical spaces where people access knowledge to digital platforms that bring knowledge directly to users. Emphasising the need to ensure the right knowledge reaches the right person at the right time, he described the ERMED Consortium’s evolution in 2024 as an important shift towards collaborative access to knowledge. He noted that access to high-quality medical and scholarly resources for clinicians, researchers, students and nursing professionals helps democratise knowledge and strengthen evidence-based decision-making.
Referring to the National Education Policy (NEP) 2020 and the One Nation One Subscription initiative, Dr. Krishna underscored the importance of technology-enabled, equitable and research-driven education, supported by wider access to scholarly resources. He emphasised that the future of medical libraries must go beyond providing information to transforming information into evidence, evidence into knowledge, and knowledge into better healthcare. This, he noted, requires a human-centred approach alongside technological advancement, with greater emphasis on AI literacy, research skills and the ability to critically evaluate information and translate evidence into meaningful action.
Looking ahead, Dr. Krishna encouraged stakeholders to envision what the National Medical Library and the ERMED Consortium should become over the next five to ten years, emphasising the need for more connected, sustainable, inclusive and responsible knowledge ecosystems. He identified access, knowledge, vision and impact as the guiding principles for the future of medical libraries, stressing that their success should ultimately be reflected in stronger medical education, research, evidence-based clinical practice and improved healthcare outcomes.
During the conference, Smt. Punya Salila Srivastava, Secretary, Ministry of Health and Family Welfare, released the National Medical Library (NML) Newsletter and Souvenir, marking an important occasion for documenting the library activities, initiatives and contributions to medical knowledge dissemination and professional engagement.
The conference focused on the evolving role of medical libraries in the digital healthcare ecosystem and the need to strengthen access to credible, high-quality scientific and medical literature. With the increasing use of digital platforms in clinical decision-making, research and medical education, the programme provided a forum for medical librarians and healthcare professionals to exchange knowledge, explore emerging practices and enhance their capacity to support evidence-based healthcare.
A key feature of the conference was hands-on training on four major ERMED resource platforms—ClinicalKey, BMJ, Access Medicine and MedOne. The training aimed to familiarise participants with these digital platforms and enhance their ability to access and utilise relevant medical literature, clinical information and academic resources effectively.
The conference also featured a panel discussion on “From Custodian to Clinical Partner: The Next Mandate for the Medical Librarian”. The discussion explored the changing responsibilities of medical librarians, emphasising their expanding role beyond the management of information resources to actively supporting clinical teams, researchers, faculty members and students in accessing and applying evidence-based knowledge.
The conference reaffirmed the importance of strengthening digital access to medical and scientific information and building the professional capacities of medical librarians to respond to the changing needs of healthcare institutions, medical education and research. Through knowledge-sharing, practical training and professional dialogue, the ERMED Consortium continues to provide a platform for advancing the use of digital health resources across the medical community.
Dr. Mukesh Pathak, Director, NML, Dr. B. Srinivas, DDG, DGHS, Distinguished Guests and Field Experts were present at the event.

title: Union Health Ministry Proposes Tighter Curbs on Advertising of Prescription Drugs by Retailers and Wholesalers
subtitle:
Draft amendment seeks to extend existing restrictions on advertisements of Schedule H, H1 and X medicines to drug retailers, wholesalers and distributors

Move aims to curb unauthorised promotion of prescription medicines and strengthen safeguards for public health
ministry: Ministry of Health and Family Welfare
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                09 OCT 2026 11:10AM by PIB Delhi
content:
The Union Ministry of Health and Family Welfare has proposed an amendment to the Drugs Rules, 1945, to strengthen regulation of advertisements relating to prescription-only medicines. The proposed amendment seeks to extend the existing requirement of prior Central Government sanction for advertising drugs specified under Schedule H, Schedule H1 and Schedule X to entities holding licences for the sale and distribution of drugs.
The draft amendment has been notified through Gazette Notification
G.S.R. 861(E), dated 28 September 2026
, following consultations with the Drugs Technical Advisory Board (DTAB).
Under the existing regulatory framework, pharmaceutical manufacturers are prohibited from advertising drugs covered under Schedule H, Schedule H1 and Schedule X without prior sanction of the Central Government. However, corresponding provisions have not explicitly covered entities engaged in the retail and wholesale sale and distribution of these medicines.
To address this regulatory gap, the Ministry has proposed the insertion of
sub-rule (22) under Rule 65 of the Drugs Rules, 1945
, extending the advertisement restriction to holders of licences to sell, stock, exhibit or offer for sale, or distribute drugs, including retail and wholesale drug licence holders.
Under the proposed provision, no advertisement of drugs specified in Schedule H, Schedule H1 or Schedule X shall be made except with the previous sanction of the Central Government.
The proposed amendment is intended to strengthen regulatory oversight across the pharmaceutical supply chain, discourage unauthorised promotion of prescription medicines and reduce risks associated with inappropriate self-medication.
The measure is expected to reinforce safeguards relating to medicines that require appropriate medical supervision, including certain antibiotics, psychotropic medicines and other prescription-only drugs.
The proposal follows the recommendations of the
93rd meeting of the Drugs Technical Advisory Board, held on 16 February 2026
, which considered the need for appropriate provisions governing advertisements by drug sale and distribution licence holders.
The Ministry has invited objections and suggestions from stakeholders and members of the public within
30 days from the date on which copies of the Gazette containing the draft rules are made available to the public
. Submissions received within the prescribed period will be considered by the Central Government before finalisation of the amendment.

https://egazette.gov.in/WriteReadData/2026/276941.pdf

title: Khadi and Village Industries: Weaving the Fabric of an Inclusive and Sustainable India
subtitle: Khadi emerges as a symbol of sustainable livelihoods, women’s empowerment and India’s rich cultural heritage
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                09 OCT 2026 12:02PM by PIB Delhi
content:
Khadi and Village Industries (KVI) have continued to play a significant role in promoting rural livelihoods, generating employment and strengthening the vision of an Atmanirbhar Bharat. Rooted in India’s rich cultural heritage, Khadi combines traditional craftsmanship with sustainable production practices and provides livelihood opportunities, particularly in rural areas.
Khadi, being hand-spun and hand-woven, is based on the use of natural fibres and local production systems. Its labour-intensive and decentralised nature provides employment opportunities at different skill levels and contributes to sustainable rural development. The sector also supports the objectives of SDG 1 (No Poverty) and SDG 8 (Decent Work and Economic Growth).
Hand spinning remains the key differentiator between Khadi and handloom. Over the years, the Khadi and Village Industries Commission (KVIC) has supported Khadi institutions through skill development, capacity building and upskilling initiatives. Measures such as enhancement of spinning and weaving wages from April 2025, support for improved working tools and infrastructure, and strengthened marketing interventions have further contributed towards improving artisan incomes and making traditional livelihoods economically sustainable.
Khadi has also evolved into a contemporary fashion and lifestyle choice. New product categories such as Khadi denim, designer saris, bridal wear, contemporary shirts and trousers have expanded its appeal among new-age consumers. The Centre of Excellence for Khadi at NIFT, Delhi has developed 2,129 Khadi design collections across multiple categories. The launch of Navyug Khadi, featuring 710 new products, and the wellness and yoga wear collection ‘Svadha’ have further contributed to the contemporary positioning of Khadi.
The Government has been supporting employment generation in the Khadi and Village Industries sector through schemes including Khadi Vikas Yojana, Gramodyog Vikas Yojana and PMEGP. Assistance is provided through financial support, working capital facilitation, quality raw materials, training, toolkits, wage support, marketing interventions, promotion of digital payments and social security measures. An evaluation study conducted by EDII, Ahmedabad, reported that more than 75 per cent of artisans across the schemes experienced a measurable increase in income following the interventions.
Khadi has also emerged as an important avenue for women’s economic empowerment and inclusive development. Around 80 per cent of approximately half a million Khadi artisans are women. Women’s participation has been particularly significant in areas such as Agarbatti, Handmade Paper, Honey Mission and Service Industries, providing them with greater opportunities for financial independence and sustainable livelihoods.
With growing global demand for handmade, traceable, natural and environmentally responsible products, Khadi and handmade products offer significant export potential. KVIC has registered as an Export Promotion Council (EPC) on the Trade Portal of the Consulate General of India in New York and has initiated efforts to facilitate greater international exposure for Khadi institutions.
The Government has also taken steps to strengthen the branding and market positioning of Khadi products. The GI tag awarded to Ponduru Khadi is expected to enhance the value realisation of its distinctive cotton and traditional spinning and weaving processes. Ponduru Khadi, Bharat Kasturi Cotton, Bengal Muslin and naturally coloured cotton products were also showcased at the inaugural BRICS MSME Forum held in Agra.
Technology upgradation and quality enhancement are being pursued alongside preservation of traditional practices. KVIC’s Central Sliver Plants are being modernised, with the plants at Chittadurga, Karnataka, and Kuttur, Kerala, having completed modernisation and becoming operational. The Chittadurga plant utilises solar energy for 50 per cent of its requirement, while wind power is being explored to further strengthen environmental sustainability. Technology upgradation of Khadi institutions and technology-based Common Facility Centres are also proposed to strengthen Village Industries clusters.
Khadi’s inherent environmental sustainability further enhances its relevance in the context of climate action and responsible consumption. Its energy-efficient and water-efficient production process, based on natural fibres and colours, contributes to a lower environmental footprint. KVIC, in collaboration with ICAR-CIRCOT, is exploring initiatives for developing naturally coloured cotton varieties aimed at reducing water use, chemical pollution and energy consumption associated with conventional dyeing processes.
Khadi also offers potential for recycling and upcycling through hand spinning, including the conversion of fibres and filaments that may not be suitable for mechanised spinning. Such initiatives have the potential to create additional employment opportunities while contributing to SDG 12 (Responsible Consumption and Production) and SDG 13 (Climate Action).
The journey of Khadi—from a symbol of Swadeshi and the freedom movement to a contemporary fashion and lifestyle choice—reflects its ability to adapt to changing consumer preferences while retaining its traditional character. By bringing together heritage and innovation, employment and entrepreneurship, women’s empowerment and social inclusion, and economic activity and environmental responsibility, Khadi continues to contribute to the broader vision of inclusive and sustainable development.
The continued evolution of Khadi demonstrates that sustainable solutions can emerge not only from modern technologies but also from traditional practices that have been preserved and refined over generations. Through its artisans, spinners and rural entrepreneurs, Khadi continues to represent a distinctive model of inclusive growth, sustainable livelihoods and responsible production.

title: NHAI to Install Retrofit Emission Control Devices on 25 DG Sets at Dwarka Expressway
subtitle:
Initiative aimed at strengthening compliance with air-quality norms and reducing emissions from diesel generator sets in Delhi-NCR

RECDs to be installed on DG sets used for the Expressway lighting and other associated operations, thereby strengthening emission-control measures during their operation
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                09 OCT 2026 4:46PM by PIB Delhi
content:
In order to strengthen environmental protection measures on National Highway corridor in National Capital Region (NCR), National Highways Authority of India (NHAI) has taken the initiative to install Retrofit Emission Control Devices (RECDs) on 25 Diesel Generator (DG) sets deployed at the 8.7 km long Package-IV of the Dwarka Expressway that connects Basai to Kherki Dhaula/Delhi-Gurugram Expressway cloverleaf intersection.
The initiative is being implemented in compliance with the directions of the Commission for Air Quality Management (CAQM) concerning the regulation of Diesel Generator (DG) sets in the NCR, with the objective of mitigating air pollution, particularly during the winter season under the Graded Response Action Plan (GRAP). Dwarka Expressway Package IV falls within the Delhi NCR region, which experiences severe air pollution during the winter months. To improve ambient air quality during this critical period, CAQM has mandated regulation and emission control measures for DG sets operating in the area.
The RECDs will be installed on DG sets used for the Expressway lighting and other associated operations, thereby strengthening emission-control measures during their operation. The implementation involves installation, testing and commissioning of the RECDs, along with comprehensive maintenance support.
The RECD installation is part of NHAI's broader approach towards integrating environmental protection into National Highway construction and operation, particularly for projects located in the NCR. The initiative will help to ensure that DG sets required for essential National Highway-related operations are equipped with appropriate emission-control systems in line with the applicable regulatory framework. NHAI has also specified that GPS-tagged photographs of RECD installations at each DG-set/locations will be maintained for verification and compliance purposes.
NHAI’s environmental initiative for National Highway projects in the Delhi - NCR are aligned with the broader objective of ensuring that the expansion and operation of National Highway infrastructure is in line with strengthening compliance for air-quality norms.

subtitle:

Redeveloped Websites offer a single-window platform for research grants, fellowships, scientific schemes and opportunities for students, researchers, start-ups and citizens, says Dr. Jitendra Singh

DBIM 3.0-compliant portals provide multilingual access in 22 languages, universal accessibility tools and seamless use across devices

Redevelopment aligns government digital platforms with common standards for branding, accessibility, security and citizen-centric service delivery
date:

content:
Union Minister of State (Independent Charge) for Science & Technology and Earth Sciences, and MoS PMO, Personnel, Public Grievances and Pensions, Atomic Energy and Space, Dr. Jitendra Singh, said that the new redeveloped websites of the Department of Science and Technology (DST) launched today reflect Prime Minister Sh Narendra Modi’s vision of citizen-first governance by making scientific information accessible, inclusive and useful to people across the country.
Emphasising the public value of the initiative, he said that its guiding principle is “Science by the People, Science for the People”, with science made available, accessible and affordable. He also stressed the importance of enabling the flow of technologies across scientific domains and industries, allowing users to identify information and opportunities according to their requirements through a common digital platform.
Dr. Jitendra Singh launched the redeveloped official websites of DST,
www.dst.gov.in
and
www.most.gov.in
, developed in accordance with the Digital Brand Identity Manual (DBIM) 3.0 and the Guidelines for Indian Government Websites and Apps (GIGW) 3.0. Prof. Umesh V. Waghmare, Secretary, Department of Science and Technology, was present on the occasion, along with senior DST officials and representatives associated with the website development initiative. The redevelopment was undertaken jointly by DST, the National Informatics Centre (NIC), the project management team and the development agency, with content curated and validated by the department’s internal divisions.
The Minister said the platform would serve students, research fellows, researchers, academic institutions, innovators, start-ups, entrepreneurs, media professionals and citizens by providing single-window access to DST schemes, grants, fellowships, scientific programmes and other opportunities. The redesigned information architecture enables users to locate relevant information more efficiently, including eligibility criteria, application guidelines, calls for proposals, awards, results and official notifications. By bringing these resources together in a structured format, the portals aim to reduce the effort required to navigate government information and strengthen public participation in India’s science and technology ecosystem.
The websites feature a standardised information architecture covering major sections such as About DST, divisions, programmes and schemes, services, opportunities, documents, and news and updates. A structured scheme and opportunity finder facilitates the discovery of research and development funding, calls for proposals, awards and application forms, while a centralised document repository provides access to guidelines, policy documents, notifications, reports and administrative forms.
Reorganised listings of DST divisions, the organisational hierarchy and officers’ contact details support easier navigation and access to relevant institutional information. The platform also provides dedicated information on bilateral and multilateral science and technology cooperation for international stakeholders.
A key feature of the new websites is the integration of Bhashini, enabling access to content in 22 languages and widening the reach of scientific information among diverse audiences. The portals incorporate universal accessibility features, including adjustable font sizes, high-contrast display modes, link highlighting, letter-spacing and line-height adjustments, and screen-reader compatibility.
Their responsive design enables access across desktops, tablets and mobile devices while maintaining readability and usability. These features are intended to make government science and technology information more accessible to students, researchers, innovators and citizens with diverse needs.
The redevelopment follows the launch of DBIM 3.0 by the Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY) in March 2025. The manual provides a common framework for the visual identity, information architecture, content presentation and overall digital presence of government ministries and departments. Complementing this framework, GIGW 3.0 establishes requirements relating to website quality, accessibility, cybersecurity, usability and lifecycle management.
The initiative forms part of the Government of India’s broader effort to harmonise its digital footprint, bringing greater consistency to government websites through standardised branding, navigation and content presentation. The redevelopment therefore extends beyond visual redesign to encompass content restructuring, improved user experience and sustainable mechanisms for digital content governance.
The websites are supported by a modular Content Management System (CMS), facilitating content updates, future expansion and integration with external science and technology applications. Security measures include SSL/TLS encryption, cybersecurity assessments and adherence to applicable CERT-In guidelines. Content Delivery Network (CDN) integration supports faster loading, system stability and service availability during periods of high traffic, including scheme-result announcements and application deadlines. The redesigned news and updates section brings together press releases, calls for proposals, results and announcements, helping users access relevant scientific information and opportunities more conveniently.
Through improved discoverability, multilingual access, universal accessibility and a standardised digital framework, the redeveloped websites seek to strengthen transparency and public access to government science and technology resources. The initiative advances a more inclusive and citizen-centric digital environment in which students, researchers, institutions, entrepreneurs and citizens can engage more easily with scientific programmes, research opportunities and technological developments.

Additional Secretary

, along with
Joint Secretaries Shri Sajeesh Kumar N, Shri Parveen Kumar Thind
,
Dr. Sandeep Rewaji Rathod, Deputy Director General
,
Smt. Pratima Gupta
and
Director
,

attended the Meeting.

effective, transparent, accountable and outcome-oriented implementation
of social justice and empowerment programmes, with particular emphasis on
last-mile delivery, beneficiary coverage and saturation, efficient utilization of resources and measurable outcomes.
He said the Meeting provides an institutional platform for a scheme-wise assessment of progress, identification of implementation gaps and challenges, sharing of best practices and formulation of
time-bound corrective and follow-up measures
to improve the delivery of benefits to eligible beneficiaries.
Shri Pant exuded confidence that the mechanism of Regional Review Meeting is expected to further strengthen the institutional framework for effective implementation of social justice, social empowerment and social defence programmes in the Western Region.
The Secretary said that the Meeting reinforces the Government's commitment to
inclusive development, social protection, dignity, equal opportunity and empowerment of vulnerable and disadvantaged sections of society
, with a continued focus on ensuring that the benefits of government schemes reach the last mile.

Pradhan Mantri Anusuchit Jaati Abhyuday Yojana (PM-AJAY)
,
measures for strengthening the enforcement machinery under the
Protection of Civil Rights Act, 1955
and the

, and the
National Action Plan for Drug Demand Reduction (NAPDDR).

physical and financial progress, beneficiary coverage and saturation, utilization of funds, institutional mechanisms, implementation of statutory safeguards, awareness and outreach measures, rehabilitation and social reintegration initiatives
, as well as convergence with the
Nasha Mukt Bharat Abhiyaan (NMBA).

beneficiary identification and saturation, inter-departmental convergence, monitoring and data management, fund utilization, grievance redressal and dissemination of best practices and replicable models
.

Scholarship Schemes, Atal Vayo Abhyuday Yojana (AVYAY)
and the
National Action for Mechanised Sanitation Ecosystem (NAMASTE).

Scholarship Schemes
focussed on beneficiary coverage, application and verification processes, timely disbursement of assistance, Direct Benefit Transfer (DBT)-related issues and measures to strengthen outreach among eligible students, particularly those who remain outside the existing coverage.
Under
AVYAY
,

NAMASTE
focussed on the identification and profiling of sanitation workers and waste pickers, occupational safety and dignity, ensuring zero fatalities during sanitation work, access to social security and health benefits, mechanization of sanitation operations, capacity building, livelihood support and convergence with other welfare and social protection schemes.
Focus on Last-Mile Delivery and Measurable Outcomes
A dedicated
Outcome Review Session

Particular emphasis was placed on
last-mile delivery and measurable outcomes
, with the objective of ensuring that government interventions translate into tangible improvements in the lives of intended beneficiaries.
The meeting identified
priority interventions and specific action points
and takeaways
for the participating States and the Union Territory, with emphasis on strengthening implementation mechanisms, improving outreach, addressing gaps in beneficiary identification and ensuring timely and transparent delivery of benefits.
Way Forward
The concluding session focused on consolidating the key observations, priorities and recommendations emerging from the deliberations. The
Way Forward
included finalization of action points and responsibilities, strengthening coordination between the Ministry, States and Union Territory Administration, time-bound resolution of implementation issues, improved monitoring of physical and financial progress and submission of
follow-up Action Taken Reports (ATRs)
by the concerned authorities.
Commitment To NMBA, Senior Citizens’ Respect & Welfare
Secretary Sudhansh Pant administered Senior Citizen Pledge and Nasha Mukt Bharat Abhiyaan Pledge, to the participants during the Meeting, reiterating adopting and strengthening the
Whole of the Government
and
Whole of the Society
approach for the Nasha Mukt Viksit Bharat and upholding and consolidation of the social values to uphold honour, dignity, welfare and healthcare of the Senior Citizenry, across the country.

title: “Accessibility Cannot Be an Afterthought”: DEPwD Calls for a Whole-of-Government Approach to Sugamya Bharat
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                09 OCT 2026 7:13PM by PIB Delhi
content:
“Accessibility cannot be an afterthought, nor can it be left to a single department or agency. It requires a concerted effort across all ministries, departments and levels of government, in partnership with civil society.” This was the central message of Ms. Manmeet Kaur Nanda, IAS, Additional Secretary, Department of Empowerment of Persons with Disabilities (DEPwD), as she called for a coordinated, whole-of-government approach to advancing accessibility across India at the consultation
“Sugamyata Ka Sankalp”
held at the India International Centre, New Delhi
.
Emphasising that accessibility cuts across education, healthcare, employment, transport, financial services and public infrastructure, Ms. Nanda stressed that progress in one sector depends on coordinated action across others. She underscored the need for States to accord accessibility the priority it deserves and for all stakeholders to work together to translate the vision of an inclusive and accessible India into reality. Her message reinforced that accessibility must be embedded at the design stage itself, rather than being added on or corrected later.
Organised by DEPwD, Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment, Government of India, in partnership with The Association of People with Disability (APD), India, and in collaboration with Ipsos, the consultation brought together representatives from government, the disability sector, academia, research and civil society to assess the progress of the Sugamya Bharat Abhiyan, identify persistent accessibility gaps and deliberate on priorities for its next phase.
Shri Girish C. Hosur, Joint Secretary, DEPwD, presented the journey and achievements of the Sugamya Bharat Abhiyan, highlighting the Department’s role in leading the initiative and advancing accessibility across public infrastructure, transport and digital services. His presentation provided the context for discussions on consolidating progress and strengthening implementation in the years ahead.
Shri S. Govindaraj, Commissioner, Office of the Chief Commissioner for Persons with Disabilities, emphasised that accessibility is the need of the hour. He highlighted the importance of the Sugamya Bharat Abhiyan in advancing accessibility across the country and stressed the need to build on the progress achieved so far to address the barriers that continue to affect persons with disabilities.
Welcoming the participants, Mr. Subir Hari Singh,  President, APD, highlighted the importance of bringing together diverse stakeholders to advance accessibility. He emphasised that meaningful progress depends on sustained partnership among government, practitioners, experts and persons with disabilities. He also outlined APD’s mission and its work in the disability sector.
The consultation featured two moderated roundtable discussions led by Ms. Tripti Sharma, Director, Ipsos. The first examined sectoral challenges in the implementation and use of accessibility data, while the second explored approaches to measuring accessibility across sectors and the essential features of a credible and practical measurement framework. The discussions underscored the importance of reliable data and evidence to guide planning, monitor implementation and assess progress.
Participants included representatives from the Ministry of Education, Ministry of Road Transport and Highways, Ministry of Information and Broadcasting, Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation, Ministry of Health and Family Welfare, Prasar Bharati and the Airports Authority of India. State Commissioners for Persons with Disabilities, representatives of the State Governments of Telangana, Andhra Pradesh and Odisha, and disability-sector leaders from across India participated both in person and online.
Launched in 2015, the Sugamya Bharat Abhiyan marked a significant national initiative to advance accessibility in the built environment, transport systems and information and communication technologies. The consultation, held against the backdrop of the Rights of Persons with Disabilities Act, 2016, provided an opportunity to reflect on achievements, identify continuing barriers and explore ways to strengthen accessibility standards, implementation and measurement.
In his closing remarks, Mr. Sukanto Aich, Chief Executive Officer, APD, observed that the gathering itself—bringing stakeholders together to learn from one another and commit to collaboration—was a sign of hope for making the vision of Sugamya Bharat Abhiyan a reality.
The consultation reinforced the shared responsibility of governments, institutions, civil society and the disability sector in building an accessible and inclusive India. Its central message was clear: accessibility must move beyond isolated initiatives to become an integral, measurable and coordinated priority across every sector.

date:

content:
Union Secretary, Ministry of Social Justice And Empowerment, Shri Sudhansh Pant inaugurated the Five-Day Geriatric Care Training Programme, at Education Hub at Kevdi Diu, in the Union Territory of Dadra and Nagar Haveli & Daman and Diu (DNH&DD), here today.
The Programme is being organized by the National Institute of Social Defence (NISD), under the Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment, Government of India, in collaboration with the Office of the Collector, Diu, Union Territory Administration of Dadra and Nagar Haveli and Daman and Diu (DNH&DD).
Joint Secretaries of the Ministry Dr Sandeep R Rathod, Shri Sajeesh Kumar N and Director NISD, Shri Gaurav Singh Rajawat, also attended the inaugural session. The Collector, Diu, Shri Rahul Dev Boora, formally welcomed the dignitaries and participants.
Speaking on the occasion, Shri Pant said the initiative seeks to create a pool of trained, sensitised and locally available frontline functionaries capable of providing basic geriatric care, identifying emerging care requirements, facilitating access to appropriate Government schemes and services, and extending emotional and psychosocial support to senior citizens at the community level.
He said the training has been suitably contextualized to address the specific needs and circumstances of senior citizens in Diu District, with a focus on strengthening locally available support systems.
The Secretary said the programme assumes particular significance in view of the evolving needs of an ageing population, including senior citizens living alone, those requiring assistance with Activities of Daily Living (ADLs) and older persons with limited access to family-based care.
Shri Pant added that the training will adopt a practical, participatory and field-oriented approach, enabling participants to translate the knowledge and skills acquired into effective support within their respective communities.
The Secretary Pant said the 5 day training training will provide participants with an understanding of the physical, psychological, emotional and social dimensions of ageing, while equipping them with practical competencies for safe, dignified and compassionate care of older persons.
The Union Secretary said the programme is expected to create a pool of approximately 50 trained and sensitized
Anganwadi Workers, frontline workers and grassroots-level functionaries in Diu District and enhance their capacity to provide basic care and support to older persons.
He said it is expected to improve the early identification of senior citizens requiring additional care or referral, strengthen awareness of Government schemes and support mechanisms, and improve community-level support for elderly persons living alone or with limited family support.
Shri Pant said this Programme represents a focused capacity-building intervention to strengthen the local ecosystem of elderly care in Diu District. He said by developing a locally available pool of trained and sensitized personnel, the initiative seeks to promote a more responsive, inclusive and supportive environment for senior citizens and contribute towards their dignity, safety, independence, social inclusion and quality of life.
The Secretary further said the Programme is  aimed at strengthening community-based support systems for senior citizens and enhancing the capacity of personnel engaged in last-mile service delivery.
Key areas will include the ageing process and changing needs of senior citizens; rights, dignity and well-being of older persons; roles of families, communities and frontline caregivers; principles of basic geriatric care; assistance with routine activities and ADLs; personal hygiene; nutrition and hydration; medication-related support; mobility assistance; safe transfer techniques; fall prevention and home safety.
The programme will also cover basic first aid and response to common emergencies, communication skills, psychosocial support, loneliness and social isolation, emotional well-being, and dementia awareness and basic caregiving approaches.
During the programme special emphasis will be placed on the prevention, identification and reporting of neglect, abuse and exploitation of senior citizens, while reinforcing the principles of privacy, dignity, respect and compassionate care.
The participants will also be oriented to Government schemes, programmes, institutional mechanisms and support services available for senior citizens, enabling them to facilitate timely access to relevant benefits and services.
The programme will combine technical sessions, interactive lectures, demonstrations, practical exercises, case studies and field-oriented examples. Group activities, experience-sharing and question-and-answer sessions will provide participants an opportunity to relate the training inputs to their field experience and develop practical responses to the diverse needs of older persons.
Practical exposure to basic caregiving techniques will form an important component of the programme, with emphasis on translating knowledge into effective community-level support.
The collaboration between the NISD, Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment, Government of India, and the Union Territory Administration of Dadra and Nagar Haveli and Daman and Diu, through the Office of the Collector, Diu, reflects a coordinated approach towards strengthening geriatric care and community-based support mechanisms at the grassroots level.
Shri Pant later administered the

Ms. Asha Sharma, Course Coordinator, and Ms. Ritu Dandriyal, Junior Consultant, from the Senior Citizen Division of NISD, are conducting the programme.
The Deputy Director (Training) & Head, Senior Citizen Division, NISD, is coordinating the programme in consultation with the Office of the Collector, Diu, and other concerned stakeholders for effective academic, administrative and logistical arrangements.
It is pertinent to mention that at the Ministry level, the NISD has been undertaking capacity-building and training programmes in geriatric care and related areas as part of its continuing efforts to strengthen the availability of trained human resources for the care, welfare and protection of senior citizens.

title: Release of Draft Guideline for Compilation Gross State Domestic Product (GSDP) Estimates by Expenditure Approach with Base Year 2022-23
date:

content:
The National Statistics Office (NSO), Ministry of Statistics & Programme Implementation (MoSPI), Government of India, has prepared the draft guideline for Compilation of Gross State Domestic Product (GSDP) Estimates from Expenditure Side with Base Year 2022-23. The guideline is being released and uploaded on the official website of MoSPI (link attached below).
The draft guideline provides a uniform and comprehensive framework for compilation of GSDP estimates from the expenditure side across States and Union Territories, with the objective of ensuring consistency, comparability and methodological standardization under the revised base year framework.
The draft guideline elaborates the concepts, coverage, data sources, estimation procedures and methodologies for compilation of GSDP from the expenditure side, covering the major expenditure components, including Private Final Consumption Expenditure (PFCE), Government Final Consumption Expenditure (GFCE), Gross Fixed Capital Formation (GFCF), Changes in Inventories, Valuables and Net Exports. At present, some States/UTs are compiling estimates of GFCF and GFCE; however, PFCE estimates are not being compiled by any State/UT. The document, therefore, provides a comprehensive framework and methodological guidance to facilitate the compilation of these expenditure components at the State/UT level.
The guideline emphasizes the use of State-specific data sources and appropriate allocation indicators for estimation of various expenditure components, to the extent feasible. In cases where direct State-level data are not available, suitable allocation methodologies and relevant indicators have been recommended for deriving State-wise estimates in a consistent and comparable manner.
The compilation of GSDP from the expenditure side provides an important complementary approach to the production/income-side estimation of GSDP and would facilitate a comprehensive assessment of economic activity at the State/UT level. The estimates would also contribute towards strengthening the State-level national accounts framework and improving the consistency of State estimates with the methodology followed at the national level.
The release of draft guideline is an important step towards harmonization of estimation practices across States/UTs and strengthening the statistical capacity of State Directorates of Economics and Statistics (DESs) for the compilation of expenditure-side GSDP estimates.
The draft Guideline is available on the official website of MoSPI (
https://www.mospi.gov.in/product/more/6-Documents
) for wider dissemination and feedback from stakeholders by 28th October, 2026

title: India and Mali commemorate World Cotton Day at United Nations Headquarters in New York
date:

content:
The Permanent Missions of India and Mali to the United Nations jointly organized an event on the theme “Cotton for Sustainability: Livelihoods, Value Addition and Partnership” at the United Nations Headquarters in New York on 7 October 2026, commemorating World Cotton Day. The United Nations General Assembly proclaimed 7 October as World Cotton Day through resolution 75/318. The observance draws attention to cotton’s role in economic development, international trade and poverty alleviation, particularly in developing and least developed countries. The event brought together Members of Parliament from India, representatives of Member States and international organizations to discuss cotton’s contribution to livelihoods, value addition and the Sustainable Development Goals.
In his welcome remarks, Ambassador Harish Parvathaneni, Permanent Representative of India to the United Nations, recalled Mahatma Gandhi’s association of cotton and the spinning wheel with self-reliance, dignity and India’s freedom struggle. He highlighted four priorities: supporting producers’ livelihoods; expanding value addition and access to markets; promoting sustainability; and strengthening technology and partnerships. He emphasized the need for affordable inputs and finance, support for smaller enterprises, and South-South and triangular cooperation to help cotton-producing countries retain more value and advance the SDGs.
Ambassador Issa Konfourou, Permanent Representative of Mali to the United Nations, highlighted cotton’s importance to Mali’s economy and rural livelihoods. He underscored the challenges posed by limited processing capacity, input costs, market access and trade-distorting support. Outlining Mali’s efforts to expand domestic processing and create employment, he welcomed mutually beneficial partnerships, including South-South cooperation, and acknowledged India as a key partner.
Asit Kumar Mal, Member of Parliament, drew on the experience of Kantha embroidery in Bolpur, West Bengal, to highlight how traditional craftsmanship adds value to cotton, supports women’s livelihoods and promotes reuse and resource efficiency. He emphasized the importance of fair remuneration, affordable credit, design support and market access for artisans.
L. K. Sudhish, Member of Parliament, highlighted Tamil Nadu’s experience in cotton knitwear and garment manufacturing, including the contribution of smaller enterprises, shared infrastructure and skilled workers. He referred to the integrated textile park being developed under the PM MITRA initiative and wastewater recovery and reuse in textile processing.
Ms. Padmini Singla, Joint Secretary, Ministry of Textiles, Government of India, highlighted India’s role as a major producer and consumer of cotton and the sector’s importance to small and marginal farmers. She outlined the Mission for Cotton Productivity and the Kasturi Cotton Bharat initiative, emphasizing improved productivity, quality and traceability. She also highlighted investments in textile infrastructure, support for artisans and small enterprises, and the importance of open, predictable trade and market access for sustainable cotton value chains.
The Permanent Representatives of Côte d’Ivoire, Uzbekistan, Chad, the Netherlands, Burkina Faso and Egypt, and the Deputy Permanent Representatives of Cameroon and Peru; Ms. Angélica Jácome, Director, Food and Agriculture Organization Liaison Office with the United Nations in New York; and Dr. Keshav R. Kranthi, Chief Scientist, International Cotton Advisory Committee, spoke on the occasion. The discussion focused on opportunities to strengthen cotton value chains, support smallholders and artisans, improve processing capacity and market access, encourage use of technology and advanced science in the sector and deepen international partnerships.
Participants also enjoyed a hands-on experience of Pen Kalamkari on cotton, guided by a master artisan from India, celebrating India’s rich craft traditions.
